push_tactic_snapshot.rationale: New course, first chapter; live probes with corrections and one application probe on the learner's own sales agent

evidence: E1: Wall-clock calculation (300 x 93 min ~ 2.7 weeks) led the learner to reclassify a distilled-start run as weeks-regime; restart cost judged by run length, not checkpoint name.
E2: Async staleness mechanism stated correctly: long rollouts span learner steps -> off-policy (Q1 definition, Rocket Fig. 4).

E3 (framework extension): Per-round training design for the sales agent: turn-local rewards (IF, naturalness, tool-calling, banned-words) remove the need to wait for episode end, bounding staleness by one round.
E4: Best-of-G prefix construction gives a same-prefix group, which makes the GRPO group baseline valid (derived right after the advantage definition was given).
E5: Valid pushbacks: a best-of-G answer can still contain an error, so error prefixes do appear in training; a judge conditioned on the full history catches cross-turn contradictions.
E6 (framework extension): Self-derived blind spot of turn-level reward: greedy per-turn optimisation under-rewards multi-turn persuasion build-up.
gaps: G1: Regime classified by name twice (distilled -> short; no distillation -> climb) before computing wall clock.
G2: Conflated staleness (numerics) with restart cost (lost time) in the sync argument.
G3: 'Each turn is fast -> little staleness' is wrong under episode-level training; valid only after the per-round redesign.
G4: Duration placed by turn count (between IF and tool use) when the stated numbers give 80-200 min.
G5: Prefix-mismatch claim (stage instructions dominate) is a hypothesis not yet measured.
rationale: Core ch-01 thesis (infrastructure follows run length; staleness vs restart as separate costs) reached after one push each. Two framework extensions on the learner's own pipeline (per-round training with turn-local rewards; greedy blind spot of turn-level reward) meet the above-bar standard. Gaps G1-G4 are real but were corrected within the session.
next_action_notes: Next: ch-02 async loop. Forward-links: per-round training design vs Rocket segment packing (ch-02); best-prefix vs single-sample rollout gap (ch-10); delayed-payoff grader without outcome reward (ch-11/12, ch-19, capstone ch-22).
